what_it_is.value: vt100 is a Rust crate that parses a terminal byte stream (through vte 0.15) into an in-memory screen — grid, scrollback, cursor, input modes — for building terminal emulators or screen/tmux-style programs; written and maintained essentially alone by Jesse Luehrs (doy).
what_it_is.note: quote: "This is essentially the terminal parser component of a graphical terminal emulator pulled out into a separate crate. Although you can use this crate to build a graphical terminal emulator, it also contains functionality necessary for implementing terminal applications that want to run other terminal applications - programs like `screen` or `tmux` for example." — [measured] README at fc26fd9 (line wraps collapsed). Authorship: Cargo.toml `authors = ["Jesse Luehrs <doy@tozt.net>"]`; the vte dependency is `vte = "0.15.0"` in the same file.

kitty_graphics.value: none. vt100 hands every byte to vte 0.15, whose state machine sends ESC _ (APC) into SosPmApcString and discards the payload without calling the performer. vt100's own vte::Perform impl and its Callbacks trait have no APC entry point, so a Kitty graphics command never reaches vt100 or the embedder; TD would have to pre-filter bytes before Parser::process.
kitty_graphics.note: quote: "0x5E..=0x5F => self.state = State::SosPmApcString," — [measured] ESC ^ (PM) and ESC _ (APC) enter the string state; line 182 routes it `State::SosPmApcString => self.anywhere(performer, byte),` and anywhere() (lib.rs:438-450) acts only on 0x18/0x1A/0x1B, otherwise `_ => ()`. vt100's `impl<CB: crate::callbacks::Callbacks> vte::Perform for WrappedScreen<CB>` (src/perform.rs:33) and Callbacks (src/callbacks.rs) have no APC method.

kitty_tags.note: [inferred] from kitty_graphics: APC is dropped inside vte before vt100 sees it. unknown: none.

sixel.value: no — vt100's vte::Perform impl defines print, execute, esc_dispatch, csi_dispatch and osc_dispatch only; DCS hook/put/unhook fall to vte's empty default methods, so a Sixel DCS is parsed and thrown away
sixel.note: quote: "fn hook(&mut self, _params: &Params, _intermediates: &[u8], _ignore: bool, _action: char) {}" — [measured] vte's default hook is empty (put and unhook likewise, lib.rs:783 and :789); perform.rs:33-239 implements no hook, put or unhook.

iterm2_images.value: no — vt100 matches OSC 0, 1, 2 and 52 only; OSC 1337 goes to Callbacks::unhandled_osc, so an embedder sees the raw params but vt100 stores no picture
iterm2_images.note: quote: "self.callbacks.unhandled_osc(&mut self.screen, params);" — [measured] the catch-all arm of osc_dispatch after `[b"0", s]`, `[b"1", s]`, `[b"2", s]` and `[b"52", ty, data]`.

kitty-keyboard: no — CSI with a > < = private marker takes the Some(i) arm and goes to unhandled_csi (perform.rs:186-194)
osc8-hyperlinks: no — OSC 8 goes to unhandled_osc and Cell has no link field (perform.rs:234-236, cell.rs:12-16)
sync-output-2026: no — decset handles 1, 6, 9, 25, 47, 1000, 1002, 1003, 1005, 1006, 1049, 2004 only; 2026 is unhandled (screen.rs:1146-1170)
osc52-clipboard: yes — copy_to_clipboard / paste_from_clipboard callbacks, added in 0.16.0 (perform.rs:210-233, callbacks.rs:27)
grapheme-clusters: no — width is per codepoint (unicode-width); zero-width codepoints are appended to the previous cell up to 18 bytes, with no UAX #29 segmentation (screen.rs:705-760, cell.rs:57)

alt-screen: yes — modes 47 and 1049 (screen.rs:1150, 1164-1168)
bracketed-paste: yes — mode 2004 (screen.rs:1169)
mouse-sgr: yes — mode 1006 sets MouseProtocolEncoding::Sgr (screen.rs:1161-1163)

performance_evidence.value: No published throughput. Memory is 32 bytes per cell, fixed by a compile-time assertion (22 content bytes, a length byte, attributes). The repository ships a replay benchmark (examples/process.rs loops 7,625 recorded frames for 30 s and prints the iteration count) and a perf/flamegraph script (bin/perf), but no results; this round did not build or run them.
performance_evidence.note: quote: "// chosen to make the size of the cell struct 32 bytes\nconst CONTENT_BYTES: usize = 22;" — [measured] and line 17: `const _: () = assert!(std::mem::size_of::<Cell>() == 32);`. Benchmark harness: examples/process.rs line 4 `(1..=7625).map(|i| {`. Throughput is unmeasured, not zero.

grid_api.value: Parser::screen() -> &Screen; Screen::cell(row, col) -> Option<&Cell> (random access; no row iterator, but rows()/rows_formatted() give per-row text or bytes). Cell exposes contents() -> &str (at most one non-zero-width char plus combining marks), is_wide(), is_wide_continuation(), fgcolor()/bgcolor() (Color::Default | Idx(u8) | Rgb(u8,u8,u8)), bold(), dim(), italic(), underline(), inverse(). No underline colour or style, no strikethrough, no blink, no hyperlink. Screen gives cursor_position() -> (row, col), hide_cursor(), row_wrapped(row), alternate_screen(), application_keypad(), application_cursor(), bracketed_paste(), mouse_protocol_mode()/encoding(); scrollback is read by set_scrollback(offset), which shifts what cell() returns.
grid_api.note: quote: "pub fn cell(&self, row: u16, col: u16) -> Option<&crate::Cell> {" — [measured] signature; Cell::contents doc (cell.rs:80-89): "Can include multiple unicode characters if combining characters are used, but will contain at most one character with a non-zero character width." The flag list is every pub fn in cell.rs; TD's renderer also wants underline colour, which vt100 does not model.

damage_tracking.value: no per-row dirty report; change is computed by diffing against a cloned previous Screen — contents_diff(&prev) and rows_diff(&prev, ...) return the bytes that turn prev into current
damage_tracking.note: quote: "Returns a terminal byte stream sufficient to turn the visible contents of the screen described by `prev` into the visible contents of the screen described by `self`." — [measured] doc of contents_diff (line wraps collapsed); Screen derives Clone (screen.rs:54), which is how an embedder keeps `prev`.

state_snapshot.value: Yes, as VT bytes, but visible screen only: Screen::state_formatted() returns escape codes reproducing the visible cells, cursor and input modes (keypad, cursor keys, bracketed paste, mouse); state_diff(&prev) returns the delta; Screen is Clone. It does not carry scrollback (the encoder walks visible_rows()), the alternate-screen flag, the primary grid under an alt screen, scroll region, origin mode, tab stops or title, and nothing is serde-serializable. That is narrower than TD's own gridwire::encode_snapshot, which already ships every scrollback row.
state_snapshot.note: quote: "Return escape codes sufficient to reproduce the entire contents of the current terminal state. This is a convenience wrapper around [`contents_formatted`](Self::contents_formatted) and [`input_mode_formatted`](Self::input_mode_formatted)." — [measured] the doc says 'entire', the code does not: Grid::write_contents_formatted iterates `for (i, row) in self.visible_rows().enumerate() {` (grid.rs:227), and input_mode_formatted documents "Supported modes are: application keypad, application cursor, bracketed paste, xterm mouse support" — no alt-screen switch is emitted. shpool relies on this for reattach (see bubble).

threading_and_loop.value: The embedder owns the loop: Parser::process(&mut self, &[u8]) is synchronous, and the crate has no PTY, no thread and no event loop (dependencies are itoa, unicode-width, vte). Parser<CB> is Send and Sync whenever the callbacks type is; no internal locks.
threading_and_loop.note: quote: "impl<CB> Send for Parser<CB> where CB: Send\nimpl<CB> Sync for Parser<CB> where CB: Sync" — [measured] docs.rs auto-trait list; parser.rs:48 `pub fn process(&mut self, bytes: &[u8]) {`; no Rc, RefCell or Arc anywhere in src/.

reply_channel.value: None built in: vt100 never writes a reply. Device attributes (CSI c), device status and cursor report (CSI 6n), DECRQM and window-size queries reach the embedder only as Callbacks::unhandled_csi(screen, i1, i2, params, c), so TD would compose and write every answer itself. Kitty a=q never arrives (APC dies in vte). It fits TD's answer-exactly-once rule — the replica installs no-op callbacks — but TD writes all reply bytes.
reply_channel.note: quote: "self.callbacks.unhandled_csi( &mut self.screen, None, None, &params.iter().collect::<Vec<_>>(), c, );" — [measured] the catch-all of csi_dispatch with no intermediate, reached by 'c' and 'n' because the match covers only @ A-H J K L M P S T X d m r t (perform.rs:104-166). Callbacks (callbacks.rs:3-67) has no reply or pty-write method.

td_migration.value: Rewrite all seven files, and end with less than today. host.rs and term.rs lose alacritty's EventLoop, Term and TermMode: vt100 has no PTY or loop, so TD writes its own read loop (keeping alacritty_terminal::tty for spawning, or taking portable-pty) and hand-builds every DA/DSR/CSI 14 t reply from unhandled_csi. socketpty.rs's EventedPty adapter only exists for alacritty's loop and would be replaced. gridwire.rs's encode_snapshot could shrink to state_formatted(), but that drops the scrollback TD ships today, so TD keeps its own encoder and ports grid_hash to vt100's Cell. pane.rs's 51 grid reads move to Screen::cell() and lose underline colour, strikethrough, hyperlinks and selection helpers. main.rs's setup_env/WindowSize and bench.rs's TermMode::BRACKETED_PASTE become small edits. Pictures still need a byte pre-filter in front of Parser::process, as on alacritty.
td_migration.note: [inferred] from TD's imports (grep alacritty_terminal in app/src at 426f072) against the vt100 API above.

biggest_risk.value: It is a sideways-to-downward move onto a dormant one-person crate (no commit since July 2025, 15 open PRs) with fewer features than the alacritty_terminal TD already has — no reflow, hyperlinks, sync output, kitty keyboard or pictures — so TD would pay a full migration and still write Kitty graphics itself.

what_it_is.value: The option that TD writes its own emulator core in-tree — grid, scrollback, reflow, modes, replies and a picture store — on top of a parser crate: vte 0.15 (Apache-2.0 OR MIT; its optional `ansi` module already decodes sequences into a Handler trait but drops APC) or wezterm's vtparse (MIT; delivers APC through apc_dispatch). Scope from prior art: Zellij's implementation (v0.45.0, PR #5428, +9,169/−125 lines in 77 files; kitty_graphics/ is 2,373 lines — parser 699, grid_state 1,149, store 269, interceptor 166, replies 51, mod 39) covers transmit, place, delete and query but not animation or Unicode placeholders. picture_anchoring.value: n/a today — TD would choose. Prior art: Zellij anchors Sixel images to a row counted from the start of the pane's scrollback and shifts them when scrollback is trimmed. Its Kitty grid anchors placements to canonical (unwrapped) lines so reflow keeps them (kitty_grid.merge_rows_into_line_start and has_placement_anchored_to_first_canonical_line in grid.rs). Its APC interceptor caps one capture at 1,048,576 bytes.

performance_evidence.note: An unwritten core has no throughput or memory figure; that is unknown, not zero. Reference points only: vt100 fixes cells at 32 bytes, Zellij's TerminalCharacter is asserted at 16 bytes on x86_64 (terminal_character.rs:929-930 at 2fce032). grid_api.value: TD would design it. TD's renderer needs, per cell: char, zero-width marks, fg/bg, underline colour, flags and wide-char spacers. Scale of the work, from prior art: Zellij's TerminalCharacter is 16 bytes (one char plus an Rc to shared CharacterStyles carrying underline_color, strike, link_anchor…) and its grid.rs alone is 6,298 lines (14,957 with character, sixel, kitty, links, selection, search and output). Warp's model directory is 22,636 non-test lines (grid/ 12,719), 16 files of it adapted from alacritty_terminal. alacritty_terminal 0.26, which TD would replace, is 11,739 lines (term/mod.rs + grid/ + cell.rs = 6,123).

damage_tracking.value: TD would build it. Prior art: Zellij's OutputBuffer tracks changed lines and serializes only changed chunks for each client.
damage_tracking.note: quote: "pub fn changed_chunks_in_viewport(" — [measured] output/mod.rs:1824 on `pub struct OutputBuffer` (:1761); grid.rs calls `self.output_buffer.update_all_lines()` (:908) to mark everything changed.

state_snapshot.value: TD would own it, and owning the core removes the one limit TD's current snapshot documents: gridwire::encode_snapshot cannot read the primary grid under an alt screen without mutating alacritty's Term. With its own core TD could snapshot structurally — both screens, scroll region, tab stops, saved cursor, pictures — or keep re-encoding VT bytes. Prior art: Zellij's Grid::serialize(scrollback_lines_to_serialize) at grid.rs:1953.
state_snapshot.note: quote: "an alt screen has no scrollback of its own and the primary grid beneath it cannot be read without mutating the terminal, so attaching to a pane inside vim shows vim exactly and leaves the history behind it empty until vim exits, when the host re-snapshots." — [measured] TD's module doc (line wraps collapsed); Zellij: `pub fn serialize(&self, scrollback_lines_to_serialize: Option<usize>) -> Option<String> {`.

threading_and_loop.value: TD owns everything: read loop, parse and locking. Today alacritty_terminal's EventLoop owns TD's PTY reader thread, parser pump and writer; an own core means TD replaces that loop too, or keeps alacritty_terminal only for tty spawning (which socketpty.rs already adapts through EventedPty), or moves to another PTY crate.
threading_and_loop.note: quote: "alacritty_terminal's EventLoop owns the PTY reader thread, the VTE parser pump, and the writer." — [measured] term.rs module doc; the PTY options are [inferred].

reply_channel.value: TD writes every reply itself, and its existing split carries over unchanged: Answers::Here (the host answers) and Answers::Elsewhere (the replica stays silent). vte::ansi hands queries to Handler methods such as identify_terminal, documented as 'should write back to the pty stream', and device_status. Zellij's own grid queues replies in pending_messages_to_pty: Vec<Vec<u8>>.
reply_channel.note: quote: "/// Identify the terminal (should write back to the pty stream).\n    fn identify_terminal(&mut self, _intermediate: Option<char>) {}" — [measured] Handler trait; TD's rule is term.rs:58-72 ("each of which must be answered exactly once"); Zellij grid.rs:834 `pub pending_messages_to_pty: Vec<Vec<u8>>,` at 2fce032.

td_migration.value: Largest of all options, because TD writes the thing it now imports. New: a core module of roughly alacritty's term+grid size (6,123 lines), plus reflow, plus pictures (Zellij's Kitty is 2,373 lines, its Sixel 489). host.rs and term.rs swap Term, TermMode and EventLoop for TD's own types and loop. socketpty.rs survives only if alacritty_terminal::tty stays for spawning. gridwire.rs's encode_snapshot and grid_hash port to TD's cell, and the alt-screen caveat goes away. pane.rs's 51 grid reads change to TD's API — the chance to shape it for gpui's styled runs. main.rs's setup_env/WindowSize and bench.rs's TermMode::BRACKETED_PASTE become small edits. The Answers::Here/Elsewhere reply design ports as is.
td_migration.note: [inferred] from TD's alacritty imports (app/src at 426f072) and the measured prior-art line counts above.

biggest_risk.value: One person takes on the long tail of VT correctness that alacritty's maintainers now carry for free — Zellij's author called Sixel alone 'many months of work', and Warp is still paying down its fork five years later — and each divergence surfaces as a pane that draws wrong, not a compile error.

bubbles.note: shpool, a session-persistence tool, uses a vt100 fork (shpool_vt100) for exactly TD's snapshot-on-attach design: README says it "continually maintains an in-memory render of the terminal state via the [`shpool_vt100`](https://crates.io/crates/shpool_vt100) crate. On reattach, `shpool` will use this in-memory render to re-draw the screen". Working host/replica prior art on a small core, and a sign vt100's upstream is slow enough that users fork (vt100-ctt, mprocs-vt100 too).
bubbles.why: Direct prior art for TD's host/window replica; worth reading for how it handles scrollback on reattach.

bubbles.note: Zellij 0.45 (2026-08) puts a 166-line byte-level KittyApcInterceptor in front of vte 0.15 — the same vte TD uses — to capture ESC _ G … ST before vte drops it (states Ground/Esc/EscUnderscore/Capturing/CapturingEsc, captures capped at 1,048,576 bytes). MIT, so TD can copy it with the notice. This is the TD-owned-read-loop design already shipped by someone else.

bubbles.note: Parser choice carries a trade-off nobody had written down: vte 0.15's `ansi` feature gives a ready Handler trait (hyperlinks, kitty keyboard modes, OSC 52, sync-output buffering in Processor, DA/DSR hooks) but drops APC; wezterm's vtparse (MIT, 0.7.0) delivers APC natively through `fn apc_dispatch(&mut self, data: Vec<u8>)` but decodes nothing above raw CSI/OSC/DCS. vte::ansi plus a Zellij-style APC pre-filter keeps both.
bubbles.why: Decides how much of an own core is TD's to write before the first line.
